claim_tested: Adg2 C terminus has a GPI attachment signal (omega, omega+2, spacer, hydrophobic tail)
key_finding: Adg2 scores 7.5; predicted omega Ser647 (ties with Ala648/Gly649/Ser650); spacer SLPPSAG..STSLQR; uncharged hydrophobic tail of 14 residues ending exactly at Phe670, mean Kyte-Doolittle 2.91
organism_assay_context: S. pombe O13854 primary sequence from UniProt REST
limitations: Omega resolved only to a 4-residue window; scorer is my own implementation, not SignalP/NetGPI/big-Pi; no external predictor could be run (EBI Job Dispatcher returned HTTP 400, fair-use block)

evidence_type: computational benchmark vs curated positives and negatives
claim_tested: The score separates GPI-anchored from non-GPI secreted, transmembrane and cytosolic proteins
key_finding: All 15 experimentally verified fungal GPI proteins score 5.5-7.5; all 6 negative controls (Sc Suc2, Sc Pho5, Sc Kar2, Sc Act1, Sp Map4, Sc Wsc1 type-I TM) return no score (no qualifying uncharged hydrophobic C-terminal tail). Adg2 at 7.5 is at the top of the positive range
organism_assay_context: S. cerevisiae and S. pombe reference proteins
limitations: 24-protein hand-curated panel; positives chosen from the literature so the panel is not an unbiased sample. Sp Gas2 (Q9USU5) is a verified GPI protein the scorer misses, possibly a C-terminal gene-model error

claim_tested: Adg2's score is extreme relative to the S. pombe proteome and the score is enriched in true GPI substrates
key_finding: Of 5,130 S. pombe UniProt entries, 0 score above Adg2's 7.5 and 14 tie at the top tier. Gold set of 17 UniProt GPI-anchor-amidated substrates: 14/17 = 82% scored. Enrichment at score >= 7.0: Fisher odds ratio 191, p = 3.5e-17. Rule score >= 7.5 and signal peptide: n = 10, precision 0.60, recall 0.35
limitations: Gold set is itself largely ECO:0000255 UniProt prediction, so this measures agreement with UniProt's pipeline, not with experiment. Precision 0.60 means ~4 of the 10 top-tier hits are likely false positives (ost1 is a clear one, tail length 21)

citation_or_source: This study, provenance/adg2_gpi_analysis.py section 1; UniProt O13854
claim_tested: Adg2 has a cleavable N-terminal signal peptide
key_finding: n-h-c architecture present: basic n-region MRRLTI (net +2), hydrophobic core at residues 8-14 (mean KD 2.36), small residues at -1 (Gly19) and -3 (Cys17) of the UniProt site. UniProt annotates SIGNAL 1-19 and CHAIN 20-670
limitations: My heuristic ties cleavage between residue 14 and residue 19 and reports 14; the cytosolic control Act1 also returns a high h-region score, so the h-region term alone is not discriminative. The UniProt site is ECO:0000255 (sequence analysis), never determined experimentally

claim_tested: The two-ended topology is conserved across Schizosaccharomyces
key_finding: Reciprocal best hits recovered S. cryophilus S9W079 and S. octosporus S9R663. Both carry a signal peptide and a GPI signal scoring 7.0 (tails 28 and 20 residues, mean KD 1.65 and 1.97). Positive control Sp Ecm33 gave z = 76-103 against the same proteomes. The S. japonicus best hit B6K1R1 is a paralog (its reciprocal best hit in S. pombe is SPCC553.10, not adg2)
organism_assay_context: S. japonicus / S. octosporus / S. cryophilus proteomes
limitations: UniRef50 lists O13854 as a singleton, so orthology rests on my own SW screen with a shuffled-protein null; no syntenic confirmation. No S. japonicus ortholog was recovered, so conservation is shown across 3 of 4 species

key_finding: A GPI cell-surface topology is functionally coherent for Adg2
organism_assay_context: adg2+ is one of seven genes induced by Ace2p, with peak transcription during septation; deletion causes defects or delays in cell separation. Co-regulated with the septum-acting enzymes Eng1, Agn1 and Cfh4
confidence: S. pombe, microarray and deletion phenotype
column10: Transcriptional and phenotypic, not localisation. The paper does not show Adg2 protein at the cell surface or test the GPI anchor

citation_or_source: PMID 16823372 (Matsuyama et al. 2006), via UniProt and PomBase CC annotation
key_finding: Adg2 resides in the endoplasmic reticulum
organism_assay_context: The ER localisation that UniProt and PomBase carry for Adg2 traces to a genome-wide YFP-tagging localisation screen, not to a dedicated study of this protein
confidence: S. pombe, YFP fusion, fluorescence microscopy
column10: An epitope tag on a protein that has both a cleavable signal peptide and a C-terminal GPI signal can block trafficking at either end; ER signal in such a screen is a known tagging artifact for GPI proteins. Cannot distinguish genuine ER residence from arrested transit

claim_tested: UniProt's own pipeline is internally inconsistent for Adg2
key_finding: O13854 carries CHAIN 20-670 with no PROPEPTIDE and no LIPIDATION feature, while the close relative SPCC1322.10 (O94549) has LIPIDATION (GPI-anchor amidated Asn) and a C-terminal PROPEPTIDE. Both have a comparable C-terminal GPI signal (7.5 vs 7.0 in my scoring)
limitations: Absence of a feature in UniProt is not evidence of absence of a GPI anchor; it shows the automatic pipeline did not fire, which is why this is a curation lead rather than a refutation

key_finding: A basic residue near omega predicts plasma membrane rather than cell wall
organism_assay_context: Proposed from a S. cerevisiae genome survey that plasma-membrane GPI proteins carry a dibasic motif just before the attachment site; assigned 20 PM and 38 cell-wall proteins on this basis
column10: Purely computational, never validated in Schizosaccharomyces

key_finding: The dibasic motif retains GPI proteins in the plasma membrane
organism_assay_context: C-terminal regions of Gas1p and Yap3p, both cited as dibasic PM-retained proteins, also target reporter cargo to the cell wall; genuine Gas1p is detected after glucanase treatment of the wall
confidence: S. cerevisiae, reporter fusions, cell wall fractionation
column10: Fusion constructs may not reproduce full-length behaviour, but the authors also detect endogenous Gas1p in the wall fraction

key_finding: The dibasic rule generalises beyond S. cerevisiae
organism_assay_context: No dibasic motif was found in any of 39 predicted H. polymorpha GPI proteins, yet 9 of 10 C-terminal GPI peptides fused to msdS delivered the reporter to the cell wall
confidence: Hansenula polymorpha, cell wall fractionation and enzyme assay
column10: Different yeast; shows absence of the motif, which is consistent with all-cell-wall rather than with the motif being non-functional where present

evidence_type: computational test of the dibasic rule on a fate-annotated panel
claim_tested: Basic residues at omega-4..omega+2 discriminate plasma membrane from cell wall
key_finding: Plasma-membrane set (Gas1 2, Yps1 0, Dfg5 0) mean 0.67 K/R; cell-wall set (Crh1 0, Cwp2 0, Cwp1 0, Sed1 1, Sag1 1, Tip1 0) mean 0.33. Mann-Whitney one-sided p = 0.439, n = 3 vs 6. Only Gas1 has an actual adjacent dibasic pair. Adg2 window SLPPSAG has 0 K/R; orthologs have 1 (S9W079) and 2 non-adjacent (S9R663)
organism_assay_context: S. cerevisiae fate-annotated GPI proteins plus Schizosaccharomyces sequences
limitations: Small n (9 proteins) gives low power; the test cannot exclude a weak effect. The conclusion is that the rule is not usable for a single-protein call, not that basic residues never matter

citation_or_source: InterPro IPR018466 / Pfam PF10342 on O13854
claim_tested: Adg2 has an identifiable functional domain
key_finding: Adg2 carries a Kre9/Knh1-like N-terminal domain, a family associated with beta-1,6-glucan assembly at the cell surface
limitations: Domain assignment is computational; S. pombe Kre9/Knh1 relatives have not been enzymatically characterised, so this constrains localisation more than molecular function
